title: (PDF) Turmeric (Curcuma longa) and its major constituent (curcumin) as ...
abstract:
- Curcumin is the primary active compound in turmeric (Curcuma longa).
- Turmeric and curcumin are considered nonmutagenic and nongenotoxic.
- Oral administration of turmeric and curcumin has not shown reproductive toxicity in animals at certain doses.
- Human studies have not revealed toxic effects, with curcumin being safe at an oral dose of 6 g/day for 4-7 weeks.
- Some individuals may experience gastrointestinal upset as an adverse effect.
- Oral bioavailable formulations of curcumin have been found safe for human consumption at 500 mg twice daily for 30 days, though further research is recommended, especially for nanoformulations.
- Curcumin is recognized as a generally recognized as safe (GRAS) substance.
- Turmeric and curcumin are generally considered nontoxic for humans, particularly when taken orally.
- Animal studies also indicate that turmeric and curcumin are safe.
- While animal studies suggest safety during pregnancy, more human studies are needed in this area.
- Acute toxicity studies in animals show curcumin to be non-toxic at doses up to 5,000 mg/kg.
- Some studies noted significant weight changes in liver tissues of mice at high doses, but no toxicity was observed in rats at similar doses.
- More extensive research is required for nanoformulations and long-term safety assessments.
